As they say, true assessment of conditions comes only after both sides have batted but the pitch has certainly quickened up on Day 2. Jofra Archer, in particular, will relish the prospect of bowling in these conditions. We did see Rishabh Pant heading out for a net session, but how comfortable he is while holding the bat remains to be seen. Since it was an external blow, he is permitted to bat at any position the team requires. For now, the tourists' first task will be to navigate the challenge of the new ball. Back in a bit for India's batting effort.

Jamie Smith continued his rich vein of form in the series, while Brydon Carse was equally impressive, bringing up his maiden Test fifty. Their 84-run stand proved invaluable, helping England forge a solid recovery after blows early in the morning. Returning to the side after a break at Edgbaston, Jasprit Bumrah was the pick of the bowlers with a sensational five-wicket haul, a performance that earns him a place on the Lord’s honours board for the first time in his career. Mohammed Siraj bowled his heart out without much luck. Smith was dropped on 5 off his bowling by KL Rahul, and Siraj eventually finished with two wickets to his name.

England have been bowled out for 387! They will gladly take that, having been in trouble at 271 for 7 earlier in the morning. The last three wickets added 116 runs and that could make all the difference when we look back at the game. Joe Root, with his 37th Test hundred, was the standout performer for the hosts. The two Bens, Duckett and Stokes, along with Ollie Pope, all got starts but couldn’t convert them into big scores.

The lower order frustrated India at Headingley, and that story seems to be repeating here as well. They will need to regroup and reset when they return after the break. It could have all gone downhill for England after those three early wickets. They were in danger of being bowled out in the first session itself. The pitch looked to have quickened up in the morning, but as the ball softened, batting became noticeably easier. England will look to push towards 400, while India will look to limit the damage. Do join us at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT) for the post-lunch session. See you then!

The English pair made merry with those tactics and ticked along quite comfortably. Although there was another change of ball later, one that seemed to please Shubman Gill this time, it did little to disrupt the rhythm of the partnership as the bowlers, apart from Bumrah, didn’t look particularly threatening. Jamie Smith, who was dropped on 5 by KL Rahul, went on to reach yet another fifty with the stand currently worth 82 runs.

63 legal deliveries into the second new ball, it went out of shape and had to be replaced. The ball selected did not sit well with the Indians, who felt it was nowhere near as new as it should have been. Mohammed Siraj and Shubman Gill made their displeasure known to the umpires, and from that point on, India appeared rattled. Despite the pressure created, they opened up the field and seemed solely focused on dismissing Brydon Carse and were happy to give easy singles to Jamie Smith.

After enduring what must have felt like one of the longest nights of his career while stranded on 99, Joe Root needed just one ball in the morning to reach his landmark. However, he couldn't stay much longer at the crease. Jasprit Bumrah gave India the perfect start to the day with a fiery three-wicket burst in his opening spell. England were reduced to 271/7 but then came that momentum-shifting moment.

SESSION SUMMARY - 22 overs, 102 runs and 3 wickets. After a serene first day at Lord’s, the morning session on Day 2 was eventful and packed with drama. England will be the happier of the two sides at this stage, having recovered well from early blows. As for India, the start was promising, but the momentum fizzled out as the session progressed.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, in all readiness for Day 2 to begin. Also, ICYMI, today marks a special occasion at Lord's. It is Red for Ruth Day, one of the most poignant days on the English cricketing calendar. This day honours Ruth Strauss, the late wife of former England captain Sir Andrew Strauss, who passed away in 2018 from a rare form of lung cancer that affects non-smokers. Led by the Ruth Strauss Foundation, the initiative raises awareness and vital funds for families facing the loss of a parent to cancer. In a powerful show of solidarity, players, commentators, and fans all will wear red. Right. The two umpires make their way out to the middle, and the Indians too, spread out of the huddle to take their fielding positions. Well then, an absorbing opening day of this third Test has flown by. It was laden with patience, grind, and of course, hard work. The surface offered subtle challenges, turn for Jadeja and the occasional uneven bounce for the seamers, keeping both bat and ball in constant contest. It was a hard-fought day that rewarded discipline and careful application over flair. With the second new ball only 2.5 overs old, the first hour of the second day promises a stern examination for Joe Root and Ben Stokes as they look to push England towards a commanding total. The Indian bowlers will be keen to make early inroads, capitalising on the freshness of the cherry to turn the tide. Day 2 begins on Friday, 11th July, and the first ball is scheduled to be bowled at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT). Till then, take care, cheers!

For a while, India held the squeeze, pairing spin and seam to keep the runs on a leash. But Joe Root was in his bubble of zen, unflustered by bounce or movement. He soaked up everything India threw at him, rarely looking hurried. Ben Stokes, at the other end, played himself in, struggling with a possible groin injury, but together they stitched another handy partnership that helped England stabilise as the shadows lengthened, and eventually coasted England safely to Stumps with an unbeaten 79-run stand.

The partnership had taken a good shape on a slow deck with the ball getting softer and softer, and conditions increasingly facilitative to batting. Come the third and final session, it just took the first ball for Jadeja to break that 109-run stand, and it was followed up nicely by Bumrah's ripper as he removed Brook cheaply, with England slipping from 153/2 to 172/4.

The second session was an absolute slow-burn, and lifeless, with the game progressing at a snail's pace. Not much happened, but the Indians were pretty disciplined with their lines and lengths. Rishabh Pant walked off the field after taking a blow on his left index finger, with Jurel coming in as the substitute keeper. Pope and Root dug in a resilient stand with the former notching up yet another fifty, with Root also crossing 3000 Test runs against India itself. Overall, with not much action, only 70 runs came in the afternoon session in 24 overs, but the Indians were deprived of wickets. Hence, uncharacteristically, the session went England's way.

Ben Stokes yet again won the toss and this time, elected to bat on a sunny, bright day in London. However, India wrested control after a cautious first hour from England, with Nitish Kumar Reddy striking twice post drinks to peg the visitors back at 44/2. Again, the English opening pair failed to bat long enough. The slower pitch and residual moisture aided movement, especially from the Nursery End, where Bumrah and Reddy thrived. False shots, uneven bounce, and fading lacquer on the Dukes ball added to England’s discomfort, before Root and Pope steadied things to close a gripping session which ended as a draw.

In this Bazball era, Root and Pope showed they can still adapt to the old-school style of Test batting when the situation calls for it. With the ball getting softer, England will know this is a phase they can capitalise on. It is now about putting their heads down after the break and cashing in on this start. In the only over bowled by Ravindra Jadeja so far, he managed to get one to rip past the outside edge and we might see spin come into play more consistently from one end after Tea. Back in a bit for the third and final session of the day.

After Bumrah and Siraj were taken out of the attack, Root and Pope looked a lot more comfortable at the crease, with Akash Deep and Nitish Kumar Reddy not posing the same level of threat. Root brought up 3000 Test runs against India on his way to a composed fifty, while Pope is closing in on a half-century of his own. In a bit of a setback for India, Rishabh Pant took a blow to his left hand while diving to stop a delivery and walked off the field with Dhruv Jurel taking over the wicket-keeping duties.

Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj resumed the attack for the tourists after Lunch and were disciplined with their lines and lengths. The duo combined well to build pressure, even stringing together a sequence of 28 consecutive dot balls at one stage. Just 26 runs came in 12 overs in the first hour, and the pressure seemed to get to Root and Pope. A few false shots crept in, but they were fortunate not to nick it behind. Despite the mounting pressure, the pair managed to hang in there.

70 runs in 24 overs. A sedate session in terms of scoring for England, but they won’t mind one bit. The wickets column remained untouched through the afternoon, and that will please the hosts. India, on the other hand, might feel a touch unlucky, having nothing to show for their disciplined effort. However, they will take heart from the fact that they made run-scoring difficult and didn’t allow England any easy runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session at Lord's. The sun is beating down and hard with not a single cloud in sight. The Indian team is in a huddle before they spread out to the field. Out walk Joe Root, 24 (34), and Ollie Pope, 12 (34), to resume their batting for England. And it will be Jasprit Bumrah (8-1-13-0) to start the afternoon session with the ball. Pope to face. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SECOND SESSION ...

Well then, an absorbing morning session has ticked by in this third Test. Come the second session, India's main aim will be to break this blossoming partnership between Root and Pope. Root, in particular, who holds a healthy average in the north of over 54, at Lord's, only second to Kevin Pietersen. And coming back after Lunch, England's primary goal will be to extend this stand and bat out through the second session, which is considered as the best one for batting. An interesting afternoon session is on the cards. Play resumes at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT). Stay tuned.

Interestingly, the conditions seemed to favour the bowlers operating from the Nursery End, where Bumrah switched his ends and from where Reddy made that impactful double strike. That particular end has consistently offered a bit more bite off the surface and through the air, with noticeable swing and seam movement. The contrast with the Pavilion End has been quite stark, suggesting subtle variations in the turf or wind direction may be playing a role in accentuating the movement.

Suddenly, the batters looked like cats on a hot tin roof, unsettled by the lateral movement and uneven bounce. A lot of edges didn’t carry, and a couple of chances went begging, including one tough grab spilled by skipper Gill at gully. With the lacquer wearing off the Dukes ball after the 13th or the 14th over, it started to talk a bit more, aided by some tackiness beneath the surface. Pope had his share of jitters but found stability through Root’s calming influence. Root’s method stood out. He simply let the ball come to him, trusting the fundamentals with a classic ‘playing the ball on its merit' approach. Unflashy, but immensely effective on a pitch that demanded patience and tight technique.

Although far from convincing, England managed to win the first mini-battle by surviving the initial hour. There were half-chances, persistent appeals, and several false shots induced, but no breakthroughs for the tourists. But, just after the drinks break, Gill's decision to introduce Nitish Kumar Reddy into the attack turned out to be a true masterstroke. Reddy landed a double blow in the same over, dismissing both openers and leaving England wobbling at 44/2.

It was indeed a testing initiation for the English batters on a slower pitch laced with early moisture, which helped the ball shape back and forth nicely. Jasprit Bumrah and Akash Deep worked hard to make the full use of the new ball, probing in the right channels and subtly adapting to the famous Lord's slope. Zak Crawley looked tentative to start with, using his feet to break the bowler's rhythm, more or less lacking some confidence while Duckett appeared a bit more composed at the crease.

SESSION SUMMARY - 25 Overs, 83 Runs, 2 Wickets. A highly entertaining opening session of this third Test. And this is just the beginning of what promises to be an enthralling match ahead. It's a shared session as the first hour belonged to the hosts, while the next one was bossed up by the Indians with the ball, constantly asking the right questions.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! England will be pleased to have seen off the first hour without losing a wicket. It was a testing period, particularly for Zak Crawley, who looked a bit edgy early on before deciding to use his feet and disrupt Akash Deep’s rhythm. That move helped him win that mini-battle. The surface has shown signs of being on the slower side, and having lost the toss, India will be eager to find breakthroughs in the next hour. As is often the case in England, the ball tends to do a bit more off the surface once the lacquer begins to wear off, and we saw it moving more in the air during Jasprit Bumrah's previous over. Commentary.Commentary: Lord’s is looking an absolute picture, with the sun shining brightly and blue skies overhead. The two umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by Shubman Gill and his men. Out walk the two English openers, Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley. Back into the side and in action straight away as Jasprit Bumrah will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for India. Crawley to face the first ball. Three slips and a gully in place. Away we go...

The two teams are battling for the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, and one of those legendary names is here in attendance. Sachin Tendulkar will ring the iconic five-minute bell at Lord’s to signal the start of play. Earlier today, the Indian legend had his portrait unveiled at the Lord’s museum. The match officials and the two teams have lined up for the national anthems. It will be the Indian national anthem first, followed by that of England.

It’s not just the men who are on an English sojourn, the women are in the country as well. In case you missed it, last night in Manchester, India sealed their first multi-game T20I series win over England. The spinners set up the win, and the tourists chased down 127 without much fuss, with three overs to spare. It is a big result for Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. ahead of the T20 World Cup in England next year. The final game of the series will be played on Saturday at Edgbaston, before both teams shift focus to the longer of the two white-ball formats, with a three-match ODI series to follow.

India (Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Karun Nair, Shubman Gill (C), Rishabh Pant (WK), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Ravindra Jadeja, Washington Sundar, Akash Deep, Mohammed Siraj, Jasprit Bumrah (In for Prasidh Krishna).
England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Ollie Pope, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Ben Stokes (C), Jamie Smith (WK), Chris Woakes, Brydon Carse, Jofra Archer (In for Josh Tongue), Shoaib Bashir.

The captain of India, Shubman Gill admits he was a bit confused about what to do but reveals he would have bowled first. Mentions that if there is anything in the wicket, it’s usually on Day 1 during the first session. Gill says it was pleasing to see contributions come from everyone across departments at Edgbaston, and that remains the aim here as well. Shares that the bowlers are feeling pretty confident. He points out that taking 20 wickets at Edgbaston was no easy task, but the attitude and effort shown by the bowling unit were outstanding. When asked about how he is feeling after his stellar performance in the last game, he replies that it is always satisfying when hard work pays off. Informs that they have made one change with Jasprit Bumrah coming in for Prasidh Krishna.

The English captain, Ben Stokes, says that the surface is as it always has been at Lord's and with the sun baking down, batting first feels good. Says that the series is on level terms and they want to leave Lord's with a 2-1 lead. On how the bodies are coping, he says it is a quick turnaround, but everyone's fresh and ready to go, as they like to play at his venue. Informs about one change in the side as Jofra Archer comes in for Josh Tongue.
TOSS - Shubman Gill calls 'heads' but it has come down as a tail. England have elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Down at the pitchside, Deep Dasgupta observes a surface that looks promising, sporting some lively grass and early moisture. He expects bowlers to get assistance regardless of the slope, suggesting a fair bit for both pacers and spinners. While it appears to be a decent batting strip too, due to sunny conditions, he reckons this pitch offers more help to the bowlers compared to the previous two games. As for spinners, he believes that they might extract some turn thanks to the slope but will likely lean on footmarks as the match progresses.

At the WTC final last month here at Lord's, pacers dominated proceedings, with 14 wickets falling on both Day 1 and Day 2. However, that had more to do with the overhead conditions than the surface, as the first two days were largely overcast. In contrast, a heatwave is expected this week. While the morning sessions may still offer some movement with a touch of moisture, conditions are likely to flatten out as the day wears on. It's all set up for an engrossing few days of Test cricket. Stick around for the flip of the coin.

For pace bowlers, the slope can either assist their natural movement or work against it. A bowler delivering from the Pavilion End may see the ball angle into the right-hander, while the same delivery from the Nursery End could shape away. For batters, it can be equally tricky. Facing from the Pavilion End, a right-hander’s head may tend to fall over towards the off side, going down the slope. From the other end, they might find themselves leaning back slightly while batting uphill.

Over the next few days, you are going to hear and read a lot about a certain five-letter word that starts with 's' and ends with 'e'. Yes, we are talking about the famous Lord’s slope. But what exactly is it, and why does it always become such a talking point whenever a Test is played here? It is a unique feature of the ground where the playing surface is not level. The pitch slopes roughly 8 feet diagonally. If you are looking straight down the pitch from the Nursery End towards the Pavilion End, the slope falls from right to left.

Across the 10 days of cricket so far, India have clearly dominated more sessions. The first Test was theirs to lose, and they did, but Shubman Gill and his men showed great character to bounce back. The tourists had their skipper leading from the front with a truckload of runs as they sealed their biggest overseas Test win by runs at a venue where they had never won before. Having been rested at Edgbaston, Jasprit Bumrah is set to return for this match, likely in place of Prasidh Krishna, with Akash Deep and Mohammed Siraj having stepped up admirably in his absence.

England have won the toss and bowled first in both Tests so far. While their chase in the opener added to the Bazball story, Edgbaston proved a bridge too far, especially with time lost to rain. Batting out a draw was their best hope, but they couldn’t hold on. Outbowled in Birmingham, they now turn to Jofra Archer for a boost. This is his first Test since the pink-ball Test in Ahmedabad in 2021. His red-ball prep has been minimal, with just one County game and 18 overs under his belt, but Lord’s is where he famously exploded onto the Test scene against Australia during the 2019 Ashes.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! The battle for the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy resumes, and it’s perfectly poised. England landed the first blow, but India came roaring back with a resounding counter-punch to level the series. Here we are at the hallowed turf of Lord’s Cricket Ground for the third Test of this five-match epic. With the two teams locked in a stalemate, you get the feeling that whoever emerges victorious here could well take charge of the series.
